title: Development and construction of piezo-driven actuator for active TS-wave control in free flight.
author: Diego Gaigher Faiçal Tardin
abstract: Because of the recent increases in both fuel costs and environmental rules, fuel efficiency is pursuit by aircraft manufacturers as never before. Among the many possibilities for better achieving this goal, there is the increase of aerodynamic efficiency by extension of laminar boundary layer. The concept of laminar flow control (LFC) has a great potential of extending the laminar boundary layer on a body, particularly on a wing. This project is intended to research the aspects of a piezo-driven actuator for active control of Tollmien-Schlichting instabilities (TS-waves) in a low-sweep wing. This actuator must be fitted for tests in TU-Berlin´s Grob G103 Twin II test aircraft. Flight tests, however, are subject to weather conditions and wind tunnel results. The tasks of this project are the following: Design and Construction of a Piezo-driven actuator; Determination of its dynamic properties with vibrometer measurements; Integration of the actuator with the test wing; Measurements of the wing´s boundary layer properties in a wind tunnel; Analysis, documentation and presentation of the results. This is part of the Unibral program, sponsored by Coordencao de Aperfeicoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (CAPES) and the Deutscher Akademischer Austausch Dienst (DAAD).
